Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Questioning the fairness of Allahabad HC's July-20 ex-parte order seeking CBI and ED inquiry into his alleged disproportionate assets, LoP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has requested Supreme Court to transfer the PIL from the high court to itself or any other HC "to secure ends of justice and preserve public confidence in the fairness of the judicial process".While challenging the validity of the HC order and questioning its fairness because of 'secret chamber hearing and sealed cover proceedings', Gandhi filed another petition seeking transfer of the PIL filed by S Vignesh Shishir from Allahabad HC to the SC or any other HC.The special leave petition, as per SC website, was filed on Aug 7 through advocate Prasanna S, registered on Aug 12 and tentatively scheduled for hearing before a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana on Aug 17.In his petition, Gandhi said proceedings before HC were among the rarest instances of a constitutional court's order being simultaneously contrary to many first principles laid down by SC. "It falls so far outside the settled contours of writ jurisdiction that to call them erroneous would be a gross understatement," he added.The Congress MP accused the high court of ordering a fishing and roving inquiry by multiple agencies against his alleged disproportionate assets through "extraordinary proceedings characterised by unjustified secrecy of in-chamber hearings and sealed cover pleadings and documents."The LoP said that HC did not even bother to issue him a notice for his response to the PIL before directing the roving inquiry and did not ascertain whether the petitioner had locus standi or bona fides, the PIL was maintainable and if the high court had the territorial jurisdiction to pass such an order.He said HC passed the order without reference to any "fundamental material" warranting such a directive.
Article Summary: LoP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has requested Supreme Court to transfer the PIL from the high court to itself or any other HC. He said HC passed the order without reference to any "fundamental material" warranting such a directive. The special leave petition, as per SC website, was filed on Aug 7 through advocate Prasanna S, registered on Aug 12.

Article Title: Opposition claims grand success, says it forced goverment to put off 5 bills
Article Text:
Ramesh said the washout mirrored the one in 2015 over the Vyapam scam, which proved nothing had improved for the youth.

(With inputs from Ambika Pandit)

NEW DELHI: Terming the monsoon session a grand success, Congress said opposition unity forced Modi govt to defer five legislations that are dangerous for the country, the most important being the one on delimitation for which BJP has been splitting parties to contrive a “tainted majority” in Parliament.AICC spokesperson Jairam Ramesh and MP Gaurav Gogoi said DMK’s support for the Tamil Nadu assembly resolution against delimitation had smashed the lies spread by BJP that it was close to winning new backing. However, Ramesh said the opposition could not be complacent because BJP had “unlimited resources” at its disposal to try new mischief.“The TN resolution is a big setback for PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah. No matter how much they try, they will never get the majority for delimitation,” Ramesh said.Congress said it had also forced the postponement of four key bills — “one nation, one election”, the 130th constitutional amendment bill on automatic dismissal of jailed CMs and ministers, FCRA and Viksit Bharat Shikshan Adhishthan.Gogoi said the passage of the mines and minerals amendment bill and national cooperative development corporation bill was a matter of concern, but some states would challenge the mines bill in court.Ramesh said the washout mirrored the one in 2015 over the Vyapam scam, which proved nothing had improved for the youth.SP MP Dimple Yadav said the insistence on a discussion on “chanda chori” was to show the country how temple donations were being looted under BJP.DMK spokesman TKS Elangovan said the PM and the home minister evaded Parliament because they were “afraid” of being caught.Trinamool Congress MP Derek O’Brien said, “This session belonged to the opposition. This was a win for the students and youth.”Congress has convened a meeting of its apex body, CWC, on Aug 19 to discuss future political strategy.
Article Summary: Congress said opposition unity forced Modi govt to defer five legislations that are dangerous for the country. AICC spokesperson Jairam Ramesh and MP Gaurav Gogoi said DMK’s support for the Tamil Nadu assembly resolution against delimitation had smashed the lies spread by BJP.

BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj alleged that Rahul indulged in "cheap innuendo and locker-room talk". India deserves a better leader of opposition than a 56-year-old man acting in a juvenile manner, she said. BJP tore into Congress for opposition MPs "bandar" jibe at Modi while protesting in Parliament complex.

Article Title: Stormy Monsoon Session fallout: INDIA bloc boycotts Lok Sabha Speaker’s tea party; DMK attends
Article Text:
File photo of SP leader Akhilesh Yadav and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Congress and SP are the two largest parties in the opposition alliance

NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc parties, including the three largest constituents of the opposition alliance — the Congress , Samajwadi Party and Trinamool Congress — on Thursday boycotted the Lok Sabha Speaker’s customary tea party held after the conclusion of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, a senior Congress leader said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi, defence minister Rajnath Singh, and several other senior leaders and ministers were present at the gathering in Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's chamber, PTI reported citing sources.Among the opposition parties, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader Kanimozhi attended the traditional get-together. The DMK, however, is no longer part of the Congress-led opposition bloc.In the Rajya Sabha, meanwhile, opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and former party chief Sonia Gandhi, attended the tea party hosted by Chairman CP Radhakrishnan.The Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman traditionally host tea parties in their respective chambers after the proceedings of the two Houses are adjourned sine die.The opposition’s decision to skip the Lok Sabha Speaker’s tea party came after a stormy Monsoon Session, marked by repeated disruptions over the Delhi Police crackdown on NEET student protesters during their march to Parliament on July 20, the first day of the session.The opposition also repeatedly demanded a government statement on the alleged theft of offerings from the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha were adjourned sine die on Thursday, the scheduled final day of the Monsoon Session.Addressing media later, Union minister Kiren Rijiju said Rajya Sabha recorded only 39% productivity, while the Lok Sabha recorded 19%.
Article Summary: Congress and SP are the two largest parties in the opposition alliance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, defence minister Rajnath Singh, and several other senior leaders and ministers were present at the gathering in Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's chamber. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader Kanimozhi attended.

Article Title: Police Nab Shop Employee, Three Others in Gunpoint Robbery
Article Text:
New Delhi:





What appeared to be a gunpoint robbery of Rs 3.5 lakh near Sherpur Chowk in northeast Delhi turned out to be an alleged inside job, with the victim’s shop employee emerging as the insider. Police have arrested three accused, including the employee, and apprehended a 17-year-old minor.According to police, the incident was reported on Aug 2. Ravi Singh Jadon told cops that he was travelling on his motorcycle with his shop employee, Mohit, carrying the cash and two mobile phones in a bag. Two masked men allegedly intercepted them on a scooter, robbed them at gunpoint and fled.A case was registered at Dayalpur police station.Police identified the accused as Mohit, 23, Aazan, 19, Shehzad, 20, and the minor. During interrogation, police alleged that Mohit had shared the victims’ live location and identified the cash bag through a gesture. Another motorcycle followed the victims and relayed their movement to the robbers.Police recovered Rs 15,000 and the motorcycle allegedly used in the crime.
Article Summary: Police have arrested three accused, including the employee, and apprehended a 17-year-old minor. Ravi Singh Jadon told cops that he was travelling on his motorcycle with his shop employee, Mohit, carrying the cash and two mobile phones. Two masked men allegedly intercepted them on a scooter, robbed them at gunpoint and fled.

Article Title: Liquor case: CBI appealed with 'haste', dismiss plea, Kejriwal and Sisodia appeal in Delhi high court
Article Text:
Arvind Kejriwal and Manish Sisodia asked the Delhi High Court to reject the CBI's rush to file a revision petition





NEW DELHI: Former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and his deputy Manish Sisodia Thursday urged Delhi High Court to dismiss CBI’s revision petition against their discharge in the liquor policy case, arguing that the same was filed with “unprecedented haste” and in the “most unserious manner”.In separate applications, the AAP founders have questioned if the CBI plea was even maintainable as it failed to show any “perversity” in the trial court’s verdict, instead seeking to “re-examine” evidence.Arguing that in a revision plea, the court has limited scope to interfere, they called the agency’s case against them as “bare-shell” and “non-specific” in the revision plea.“The present revision petition was filed only within four hours of passing of the order of discharge, which manifestly shows non-appreciation of the findings of the special judge in the discharge judgment running into more than 500 pages,” the application highlights.“That due to filing of such bare-shell, omnibus and non-specific petition — a grave prejudice is caused to the respondent,” they said.Justice Manoj Jain is scheduled to hear on Aug 17 and 18 CBI’s petition assailing the trial court’s Feb 27 decision. On the last date of hearing, Justice Jain had granted a final opportunity to Kejriwal, Sisodia and Durgesh Pathak , another AAP functionary, to respond to the plea within two weeks.Kejriwal and Sisodia asserted that the trial court discharged all accused after hearing the matter in detail for more than three months, but CBI had not pointed out any specific finding that was “perverse” or showed any irregularity, and merely pointed out “self-serving facts”.Kejriwal and Sisodia also emphasised, “The revision petition seeks re-narration and re-examination of evidence... The said exercise cannot be done in the revisional jurisdiction.”On Feb 27, the trial court discharged Kejriwal, Sisodia and 21 others, ruling that the case was unable to survive judicial scrutiny and stood discredited in its entirety.In its nearly 1,000-page revision petition, CBI contended that the trial court had conducted a “mini-trial” at the stage of framing of charges and passed the discharge order on a “selective reading of the prosecution case”.
Article Summary: Former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and his deputy Manish Sisodia Thursday urged Delhi High Court to dismiss CBI’s revision petition against their discharge in the liquor policy case. They argued that the same was filed with “unprecedented haste” and in the “most unserious manner’

Article Title: UK businessman re-arrested in fresh cheating case after securing bail
Article Text:
Mumbai:





Nishit Patel, a UK-based businessman who was granted conditional bail from a sessions court on Wednesday in a cheating case, has been arrested in another case by the police.He was granted bail in a case where he along with others was accused of duping actor Javed Jaffrey and his wife of Rs 17 crore. Soon after his release from Arthur Road Jail, Patel was arrested by the police .In the fresh case, police arrested Patel for allegedly cheating a luxury watch dealer of over Rs 92 lakh by taking delivery of three high-end watches and failing to make the promised payments. The complainant alleged that on February 13, Patel selected a Hublot watch worth ₹Rs 18.65 lakh and a Franck Muller watch worth Rs 19.38 lakh.The complaint further stated that Patel returned to the shop on February 14 and purchased another Franck Muller watch valued at Rs 54.49 lakh. He allegedly assured the shop that the payment would be made immediately through RTGS. However, the RTGS payment was never received.Meanwhile, in the Jaffrey cheating case, the Bombay high court has granted interim protection from arrest to assistant commissioner Mahesh Patil, one of the accused. Patil has approached the high court seeking anticipatory bail, contending that he is ready to turn approver.
Article Summary: Nishit Patel, a UK-based businessman who was granted conditional bail from a sessions court on Wednesday in a cheating case, has been arrested in another case by the police. He was granted bail in a case where he along with others was accused of duping actor Javed Jaffrey and his wife of Rs 17 crore. Soon after his release from Arthur Road Jail, Patel was arrested by thePolice.

Article Title: Bombay high court refuses to quash criminal proceedings against Akbaruddin Owaisi
Article Text:
Justice Joshi observed that an elected representative was expected to understand the consequences of such comments and that the speech appeared “planned”, “measured” and “predetermined”.

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high court has refused to quash criminal proceedings against AIMIM MLA Akbaruddin Owaisi over a speech delivered at a 2011 election rally in Nanded saying that freedom of speech is not an unfettered right and cannot be used to deliberately hurt religious sentiments.In an order passed on Aug 6, Justice R M Joshi dismissed Owaisi’s plea challenging the FIR, chargesheet and a magistrate’s 2021 order issuing process under sections 295A and 298 of the Indian Penal Code. The case stems from a complaint filed by BJP MLA Rajasingh T Naval Singh Lodh, who alleged that Owaisi made derogatory remarks against Lord Ram and members of his community.Rejecting Owaisi’s contention that the case was barred by limitation, the court relied on the Supreme Court’s 2025 ruling in Ghanshyam Soni vs State (Govt of NCT of Delhi) and held that limitation is computed from the date of filing of the complaint or initiation of proceedings, not from the date cognisance is taken.The court noted that Owaisi’s speech was delivered on Dec 8, 2011, while the complaint was filed within the prescribed period. It further held that the charge under section 298 could proceed along with the more serious offence under section 295A.Examining the substance of the speech, Justice Joshi observed that Owaisi initially referred to the Allahabad high court’s Ram Janmabhoomi judgment but later made remarks which, prima facie, appeared intended to mock Lord Ram and wound the sentiments of his followers.The court declined to reproduce the alleged remarks to avoid further publicity but said the statements appeared to be neither casual nor spontaneous.Justice Joshi observed that an elected representative was expected to understand the consequences of such comments and that the speech appeared “planned”, “measured” and “predetermined”.Referring to the ingredients of section 295A, the court said deliberate and malicious intent must be assessed in the context of the words used as well as their tone, pitch and manner of delivery.“Tolerance cannot be misconstrued/misunderstood to there being a licence to intentionally hurt the religious feelings of others,” Justice Joshi observed.The court further said constitutional values such as liberty, tolerance and fraternity do not provide protection for deliberate acts intended to outrage religious sentiments. It distinguished judgments cited by the defence, noting that those cases lacked allegations or evidence of deliberate and malicious intent. In contrast, the material placed on record in the present case prima facie indicated apparently outrageous statements and a triable case, it noted.The court also took note of the prosecution’s submission that the speech continues to be available online, calling it a serious concern as it could perpetuate the alleged insult. While refraining from issuing directions in the absence of necessary parties, the court expressed hope that govt would take appropriate action.Dismissing the petition, the high court clarified that its observations were only prima facie and should not influence the trial court while deciding the case on merits.
Article Summary: The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high court has refused to quash criminal proceedings against AIMIM MLA Akbaruddin Owaisi. The case stems from a complaint filed by BJP MLA Rajasingh T Naval Singh Lodh, who alleged that O Waisi made derogatory remarks against Lord Ram and members of his community.

Article Title: ​Farmer dies of snake bite in Sillod
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A 60-year-old farmer, Vitthal Abaji Mirge, died after being bitten by a venomous snake at Asadi village in Sillod taluka of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district on Wednesday.According to investigating officer Vaijnath Chavan, Mirge was working in a cowshed when the snake bit him around 10am. Sillod rural police have registered a case of accidental death in connection with the incident.“According to family members, Chavan was first taken to a private hospital where the doctor referred him to the sub-district hospital in Sillod where the stock of anti-venom was available. Doctors at the sub-district hospital offered necessary treatment and asked family members to take Chavan to the Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar owing to his worsening health,” he said.The family tried to take the farmer to the GMCH, but he passed away on the way. GMCH authorities said the farmer was brought dead.When contacted, Dr Ram Mohite, medical officer with Sillod sub-district hospital, said the farmer was administered with the anti-venom. “We have had sufficient stock of anti-venom and the farmer was given necessary medication. As he was not responding to the treatment, we asked the family members to shift the patient to the GMCH,” he said.“The farmer was brought to the sub-district hospital with considerable delay. The family members first went to a private hospital and then came to our hospital. The delay in getting the life-saving medicine might have led to his death,” he said.The zilla parishad administration earlier in July had announced that all govt rural hospitals have adequate stock of the anti-venom.
Article Summary: 60-year-old farmer Vitthal Abaji Mirge died after being bitten by a venomous snake. Mirge was working in a cowshed when the snake bit him around 10am. Sillod rural police have registered a case of accidental death in connection with the incident.

Article Title: Another job fraud case against arrested man
Article Text:
The Parvati police registered a case of cheating against Shivanand Patil on Wednesday

Pune:

TOI





A Dhayari resident (35) has lodged a complaint against an already arrested man from Karvenagar, alleging that he cheated him of Rs 15 lakh by promising him a job as a junior engineer with Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC).The Parvati police registered a case of cheating against Patil on Wednesday. The complainant currently works with a private engineering company.The cheating took place between Dec 2023 and July. The suspect allegedly gave the complainant a fake PMC appointment letter earlier this year. When the complainant approached PMC with the letter, officials informed him that it was a fake.Rajendra Sahane, senior inspector of Parvati police station, told, “The Shivajinagar police have already arrested the suspect, Shivanand Patil (45) in a similar job fraud case.”“So far, four separate job fraud cases have been registered against him,” Sahane said.
Article Summary: A Dhayari resident (35) has lodged a complaint against an already arrested man from Karvenagar. The Parvati police registered a case of cheating against Shivanand Patil on Wednesday. The suspect allegedly gave the complainant a fake PMC appointment letter earlier this year.

Article Title: Three held for extorting building contractor
Article Text:
Pune:





Dehu Road police on Wednesday arrested three men on the charge of extorting money from a building contractor by threatening to stop his construction work. The accused also allegedly forcibly occupied one of the flats in the building and demanded Rs 3 lakh from him to vacate it, an officer from the Dehu Road police said.The trio has been charged under sections 308 ( extortion ), 351 (criminal intimidation) and 61 (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). A 44-year-old building contractor from Thergaon lodged a complaint against the trio.An officer from the Dehu Road police said the complainant was constructing a residential building at Mamurdi. Since Feb this year, the trio had allegedly been harassing him with the help of some locals, forcing him to stop the construction work. “The trio had taken Rs50,000 from him to help restart the work,” the officer said. He said the trio later threatened to stop the complainant’s work again and allegedly extorted Rs7 lakh from him at regular intervals. They were also demanding an additional Rs5 lakh from him, of which they allegedly recovered Rs2.5 lakh through a cheque. “One of them then threatened to implicate the complainant in a false Atrocities case and demanded Rs9.7 lakh more from him,” he said.The officer said that after the building was completed, the accused allegedly forcibly occupied one of the flats and demanded Rs 3 lakh from the complainant to vacate it. Frustrated by the harassment, the building contractor approached the police on Wednesday and lodged a complaint. “Our investigation is underway,” the officer said.
Article Summary: The trio has been charged under sections 308 ( extortion), 351 (criminal intimidation) and 61 (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) A 44-year-old building contractor from Thergaon lodged a complaint against the trio.

Article Title: Mobile technician shares woman’s private pics
Article Text:
Nagpur:





MIDC police have registered a case against a 26-year-old technician who repaired mobile phones for allegedly accessing and displaying private photographs and videos of a woman and her husband.As per the 32-year-old complainant, who is a caterer, she had stored personal photographs and videos of her modelling days before marriage on her mobile phone.On August 9, the phone’s touchscreen stopped functioning. She took it to a shop on Hingna Road in MIDC area for repairs. The accused, Sunny Singh , a resident of Ram Nagar, asked her for the screen lock pattern and gave her an old mobile to use temporarily.A few days later, the complainant learnt from shop workers that Singh had viewed the private images and videos of the woman and her husband, and shown them to other employees.When she confronted him, Singh allegedly used filthy language and threatened the woman. She approached Hingna police, who registered the offence on August 10 under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for outraging modesty of a woman, intentional insult, criminal intimidation and related offences. Police said the accused is yet to be arrested.
Article Summary: The 32-year-old complainant had stored personal photographs and videos of her modelling days before marriage on her mobile phone. She took it to a shop on Hingna Road in MIDC area for repairs. The accused, Sunny Singh, a resident of Ram Nagar, gave her an old mobile to use temporarily.

Article Title: Ashramshala snakebite deaths: Principal, hostel superintendent arrested
Article Text:
Gadchiroli ashramshala

Nagpur:





Police on Thursday made the first arrests in the Gadchiroli ashramshala snakebite deaths case, taking into custody principal Prashant Tatpalliwar and hostel superintendent Bhaskar Bhoyar, less than 24 hours after naming them in an FIR.Gadchiroli SP M Ramesh confirmed the arrests in connection with the deaths of three tribal girl students at Japatlai ashramshala in Dhanora taluka on Aug 10.Dhanora police have registered crime No. 86 under provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Juvenile Justice Act. Besides Tatpalliwar and Bhoyar, the FIR names woman hostel superintendent Bhagyashree Chinlamwar and members of trust management, which runs the ashramshala, Marotrao Kowase and his son Vishwajeet, as co-accused.Earlier, the govt initiated the process to cancel permission of Japatlai ashramshala after the snakebite deaths and ordered an audit of 533 aided ashramshalas in the state.Reacting to the development, Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar alleged that the monthly grant of Rs2,000 per student for ashramshalas has remained unchanged since before 2014. “Ashramshalas are expected to cover food, books, clothing, oil and other necessities despite a sharp rise in prices over the years,” he said, adding that the cost of cooking oil alone had increased from around Rs70 per litre to nearly Rs200 per litre during the period.
Article Summary: Principal Prashant Tatpalliwar and hostel superintendent Bhaskar Bhoyar arrested. Three tribal girl students died of snakebite at Japatlai ashramshala in Dhanora taluka. Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar alleged that the monthly grant of Rs2,000 per student for ashrams has remained unchanged since before 2014.

Article Title: 2 Bangladeshi nationals held for illegal entry
Article Text:
Nashik:

TOI





The crime branch (unit 2) of Nashik city police arrested two Bangladeshi nationals who illegally entered India and were preparing to travel to Pune via Nashik.Acting on the directives of commissioner of police Sandeep Karnik and DCP (crime) Kiran Kumar Chavan to track foreign nationals staying illegally in the city, head constables Pradeep Nannavare and Santosh Supekar, in the course of gathering information, had received confidential intelligence regarding the suspects.The informer told the police that a man and a woman, both Bangladeshi nationals, had infiltrated into India and were present at the Nashik Road bus stand to catch a bus to Pune. Soon after getting the information, the constables contacted their senior officials, after which a team was prepared and a trap was laid near the police chowky at the Nashik Road bus stand. The suspects were later arrested.They have been identified as Mohammad Sakib Mulla (22) and Nahida Badshah Mulla (29), both from Narail district in Khulna state of Bangladesh.Upon questioning, neither of them could produce valid travel documents or passports and confessed to crossing the India-Bangladesh border illegally.A case has been registered at the Nashik Road police Station on behalf of govt following a complaint filed by Supekar.Chavan, while talking to, said people from Bangladesh generally intrude into India to seek employment. “Nonetheless, the case is being investigated,” he said.
Article Summary: Two Bangladeshi nationals illegally entered India and were preparing to travel to Pune via Nashik. Mohammad Sakib Mulla and Nahida Badshah Mulla, both from Narail district in Khulna state of Bangladesh, were arrested.

Article Title: Gudiyattam woman head constable stabbed to death by husband
Article Text:
Vellore:





A woman head constable attached to Gudiyattam taluk police station was stabbed to death, allegedly by her husband, while she was returning home after duty near Nellorpettai on the Gudiyattam-Pernambut road on Thursday night.The head constable, A Thamaraiselvi of Erthangal was riding home on her two-wheeler around 8 pm when her husband, Arvindan, an auto driver, intercepted her. Police said he stabbed her on the neck with a pair of scissors before fleeing the spot. Thamaraiselvi collapsed in a pool of blood on the road.Passersby rushed Thamaraiselvi to the govt hospital in Gudiyattam, where doctors declared her brought dead. Arvindan later went to the same hospital and got admitted claiming that he was also injured. Police said Arvindan had inflicted injuries on his chest using the same scissor. He is being questioned in the hospital.Police said the couple, with two children, had been having frequent arguments over a family dispute for the past few days.A case has been registered and further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Head constable A Thamaraiselvi of Erthangal was riding home on her two-wheeler. Her husband, Arvindan, an auto driver, intercepted her. Police said he stabbed her on the neck with a pair of scissors.

Article Title: Vijay urges Modi to freeze LS strength
Article Text:
C Joseph Vijay

Chennai:





Chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging the Union govt to permanently freeze the strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 and protect the existing level of parliamentary representation of the states.“The existing number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to the states should be made permanent at the current level. Current distribution of seats among the States must be maintained. I kindly request you to consider the resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and bring in necessary Constitutional amendments in this regard,” Vijay said in the letter.The resolution in the state assembly was backed by DMK and coalition partners of TVK, while AIADMK, PMK, DMDK and BJP opposed it. The resolution also wanted the Union govt to implement 33% reservation for women without increasing the number of seats from the present level.“I wish to bring to your kind attention the deliberations of the Tamil Nadu assembly on the issue of proposed delimitation of parliamentary and state assembly constituencies and the implementation of 33% reservation for women,” Vijay said.He said the delimitation exercise based on population will result in a reduction in the number of seats to the southern states. “Any delimitation based on post-1971 population that alters the existing strength would cause lasting injustice to the southern states which have efficiently implemented the population control programmes, achieved good economic growth, carried out proper healthcare and public welfare schemes,” Vijay said.
Article Summary: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging the Union govt to permanently freeze the strength of the Lok Sabha at 543. The resolution in the state assembly was backed by DMK and coalition partners of TVK. AIADMK, PMK, DMDK and BJP opposed it.

Article Title: No civic polls in Pondy for 14 years: Hold it expeditiously, rules HC
Article Text:
Chennai:





Noting that no local body elections had been held in the Union territory of Puducherry for about 14 years, a former MP from the UT moved Madras high court seeking direction to the territorial administration to expedite the civic poll process.Disposing of the plea moved by M Ramadoss, president of the Puducherry Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam, the first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan directed Puducherry govt on Thursday to ensure that the process is completed as expeditiously as possible.Responding, Puducherry govt submitted that it is conscious of the constitutional importance of elected local bodies and has no intention to delay local body elections. However, the conduct of local body elections must be preceded by a legally sustainable reservation framework. A one-man-commission constituted for the purpose has submitted its report and govt is progressing the matter, it said.“The office of the state election commission is vacant and upon finalisation of the reservation framework, the same will be transmitted to the state election commission for allotment and rotation of reserved wards. It will take consequential steps for conduct of local body elections in accordance with law, for which 24 months time is required,” the govt said. It added that the report of the commission requires detailed scrutiny before any final reservation notification is issued.Recording the submissions, the bench passed the order.
Article Summary: No local body elections had been held in the Union territory of Puducherry for about 14 years. A former MP from the UT moved Madras high court seeking direction to the territorial administration to expedite the civic poll process. The first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan passed the order.

Article Title: Cop arrested for accepting Rs 30,000 bribe from farmer near Namakkal
Article Text:
Representative image





NAMAKKAL: Sleuths of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) have arrested a special sub-inspector (SSI) attached to Nallur police station in Namakkal district on charges of accepting a bribe of Rs 30,000 to settle a land encroachment case.SSI V Gangadharan demanded Rs 30,000 from K Saumiyaraj, 47, a farmer in Nadandhai Salappalayam, to close a land encroachment case registered against him and his neighbour, S Muthusamy, 48, four months ago.Unwilling to pay the bribe, Saumiyaraj lodged a complaint with the DVAC unit in Namakkal on Tuesday. Acting on the complaint, officials instructed him to hand over chemical-coated currency notes to the tune of Rs 30,000 to the SSI.On Tuesday evening, as Saumiyaraj handed over the cash to Gangadharan, DVAC sleuths led by inspector Prabhu caught him red-handed. “He was arrested and taken into custody for interrogation,” said a DVAC officer.
Article Summary: SSI V Gangadharan demanded Rs 30,000 from K Saumiyaraj, 47, a farmer in Nadandhai Salappalayam. DVAC sleuths led by inspector Prabhu caught him red- handed.

Article Title: 12 workers injured as church construction collapses in Thoothukudi
Article Text:
As many as 12 workers suffered minor injuries as the concrete portion of a church which was under collapsed in Thoothukudi on Thursday

Madurai:





Twelve workers suffered minor injuries after a portion of a church under construction collapsed at Vellapatti near Thalamuthu Nagar in Thoothukudi district on Thursday.Construction work was under way at Our Lady of Good Counsel Church when the iron rods supporting a newly laid concrete roof portion slipped, causing part of the structure to collapse. The workers were trapped under the debris.Fire and rescue services personnel rushed to the spot and rescued all 12 workers. They were taken to the government medical college hospital in Thoothukudi for treatment.Thalamuthu Nagar police registered a case and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: Construction work was under way at Our Lady of Good Counsel Church when the iron rods supporting a newly laid concrete roof portion slipped. Fire and rescue services personnel rushed to the spot and rescued all 12 workers. They were taken to the government medical college hospital in Thoothukudi for treatment.

Article Title: Former VAO arrested in Meenakshi temple land case
Article Text:
Former tahsildar of Paramakudi, Anbalagan, who was arrested in connection with the case pertaining to the alleged transfer and register of property worth approximately Rs60 crore belonging to the Madurai Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple

Madurai

:





Cleared/130 WordsCentral Crime Branch (CCB) police have arrested former village administrative officer (VAO) Arasan in connection with the case pertaining to the alleged transfer and register of temple property worth approximately Rs60 crore belonging to the Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple in Madurai.Arasan was arrested as part of the continuing investigation. Police questioned him before producing him in court, which remanded him in judicial custody.Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu government has suspended deputy collector of Ramanathapuram district and former tahsildar of Paramakudi, Anbalagan, who was arrested in connection with the case.The CCB, which is probing the case, had earlier arrested Rajkumar from Pudukottai, Ilaiyaraja from Usilampatti, and Anbalagan.In the latest development, the CCB arrested Kalikumar, a resident of Thenmalai village in Sirumalai, Dindigul district, as the fourth accused in the case.
Article Summary: Arasan was arrested as part of the continuing investigation. Police questioned him before producing him in court, which remanded him in judicial custody. Tamil Nadu government has suspended deputy collector of Ramanathapuram district and former tahsildar of Paramakudi, Anbalagan, in connection with the case.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Man held for thefts from parked cars
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The Ernakulam Central Police on Thursday arrested a 49-year-old man for allegedly stealing valuables from two parked cars after breaking the windows of the vehicles.The accused, Sharath of Puliyarakkonam in Thiruvananthapuram, allegedly targeted cars parked on MG Road and Banerji Road on Aug 5.The probe was conducted under the supervision of Ernakulam central assistant commissioner Sibi Tom. The investigation team examined CCTV footage and reviewed similar previous cases.The police said Sharath went into hiding in the Guruvayur area. He was arrested with assistance from Guruvayur Police.The investigation team included sub-inspectors Harikrishnan and Shaji, senior civil police officers Prasanth Babu and Vipin, and civil police officers Harish Babu and Rinu.Officers said the accused was involved in several similar cases. He was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The Ernakulam Central Police on Thursday arrested a 49-year-old man for allegedly stealing valuables from two parked cars. The accused, Sharath of Puliyarakkonam in Thiruvananthapuram, allegedly targeted cars parked on MG Road and Banerji Road.

Article Title: Tripunithura Athachamayam procession on Sunday
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The 10-day Onam celebrations in Tripunithura will begin with Athachamayam procession on Sunday. The celebrations will be inaugurated by chief minister V D Satheesan, whereas actor Manoj K Jayan will flag off the procession.According to municipality chairperson P L Babu, the procession will be conducted adhering to green protocols and will feature traditional art forms including kathakali, pulikali, chendamelam and theyyam, with celebrations set to continue till Aug 25.According to Babu, the civic body has made arrangements for the large crowd expected for the event. Around 500 police personnel and volunteers will be deployed for security and traffic management. Parking facilities have been arranged at six locations, including the Sanskrit College ground, Sanskrit School ground, Govt Girls Higher Secondary School ground, NSS College ground, Karingachira Church ground and Sree Venkiteswara School ground.The inaugural ceremony and flag hoisting will be held at the Govt Boys Higher Secondary School ground at 9am. Tripunithura MLA Deepak Joy will preside over the function.Civil supplies minister Anoop Jacob will hoist the ‘atham’ flag. Ernakulam MP Hibi Eden, Kottayam MP Francis George and Ernakulam district collector G Priyanka will attend as chief guests.According to municipality officials, for the procession, the municipality has ensured drinking water, toilets and medical assistance. Five ambulances will be stationed at different locations in Tripunithura. Public toilets will be available near the Poornathrayeesa temple, and Vadakkekotta and SN Metro stations.
Article Summary: The 10-day Onam celebrations in Tripunithura will begin with Athachamayam procession on Sunday. The celebrations will be inaugurated by chief minister V D Satheesan, whereas actor Manoj K Jayan will flag off the procession.

Article Title: Roji Augustine appears before court in cheating case
Article Text:
Muttil tree felling





Kochi: Roji Augustine, the prime accused in a ‘cheating case’ linked to the controversial tree felling at Muttil in Wayanad in 2020-21, appeared before Chottanikkara JFCM court in Ernakulam on Thursday. His brothers Josekutty and Anto had appeared before the court on Tuesday evening after it issued non-bailable warrants against them on Monday. The three are key accused in the large-scale illegal felling of trees in Muttil. The felling of rosewood trees in revenue patta lands of Muttil south village allegedly occurred in Nov-Dec 2020 and Jan-Feb 2021.There was a specific court directive that all the accused must be present for the hearing on Monday, and the court issued non-bailable warrants after they failed to appear for the framing of charges. The court has vacated the warrants after their appearance.The case pertains to the FIR registered by Ambalamedu Police on a petition filed by MM Aliyar, proprietor of Malabar Timber Industries, Karimugal, who had alleged fraud in the sale of timber from the illegally felled trees in 2021. In July, HC dismissed the discharge petitions filed by Josekutty and Anto. The allegation is that they cheated Aliyar of Rs 1.4 crore and the FIR was registered on July 13, 2021.The FIR was registered under IPC Sections 406 (criminal breach of trust) and 420 (cheating). The high court quashed the charge under IPC Section 406.
Article Summary: Roji Augustine, the prime accused in a ‘cheating case’ linked to the controversial tree felling at Muttil in Wayanad in 2020-21, appeared before Chottanikkara JFCM court in Ernakulam. His brothers Josekutty and Anto had appeared before the court on Tuesday evening after it issued non-bailable warrants against them on Monday. The three are key accused in the large-scale illegal felling of trees in Muttil.
